description: Big outlines: find the spine, engine, and order of a piece before any prose exists — from an essay's one-sentence claim to a novel's beat sheet and scene list, an act structure, or an essay skeleton. Use when material exists (fragments, notes, a bible, a premise) but the sequence or structure is unsettled; when a draft rambles for lack of a controlling claim; when the user says outline, structure, plot, beat sheet, chapter map, or act breaks. Write no prose — prose is writing-draft's job.
